articles.title: Gaza strike kills two Doctors Without Borders staff Israel links to Hamas
articles.description: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) voiced outrage on Saturday after an Israeli strike killed two staff members at a clinic in Gaza, while the Israeli military said the pair were Hamas "terrorists". The Friday night strike in Gaza City drew swift condemnation from the head of the UN's World Health Organization and came despite a ceasefire in the war-shattered Palestinian territory.

related.title: Israeli strike on Gaza kills two medics from Doctors Without Borders

articles.title: France and seven other countries call for Palestinian elections in early 2027
articles.description: France and seven other countries including the UK and Canada on Saturday urged the Palestinian Authority to hold its delayed parliamentary and presidential votes by the end of March 2027. They criticised Mahmoud Abbas's move to push both back to September and made their continued support for the PA conditional on democratic reform.

articles.title: ‘Pacman’ of the French Presidential Race
articles.description: David Lisnard is the darkhorse emerging from the pack in the French Presidential race. The Conservative Mayor of Cannes has so far runs a successfully social media campaign, with the hashtag #ilsepassquelquechose (Something is Happening). it appears to be causing the consternation amongst the front runners. The 57 year old, who invokes Margaret Thatcher as a key inspiration, has been taking the flak from all sides this week.

articles.title: Ukraine restricts reporting on impact of Russian strikes
articles.description: Ukraine on Saturday said it would restrict media outlets from publishing details about the impact of Russian strikes on critical infrastructure, as Moscow steps up its bombardments ahead of winter. "The idea is to maximize the difficulty that the Russians will have in understanding how successful their hits have been," FRANCE 24's Ukraine correspondent Gulliver Cragg said, reporting live from Kyiv.

articles.title: Israel's Netanyahu proposes rival Eisenkot serve as first PM in rotating premiership
articles.description: Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday offered to make way for opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, saying his rival could take office first if the two agree to alternate as prime minister. Netanyahu said threats to the country's very existence justified dropping the custom that the biggest party leads the government.

articles.title: Three days in the dark: How prepared are we for the lights to go out?
articles.description: Authorities are urging households to prepare for 72 hours without power, water or internet access as cyberattacks, infrastructure failures and extreme weather expose France and other countries to national security vulnerabilities. The message is of practical resilience, not alarm: modest preparations can help keep people safe when essential services falter – and recent security breaches are sparking a wider reckoning across Europe, including France's presidential campaigns.

articles.title: Live: Ukraine downs Russian drone with laser technology as Moscow intercepts overnight assault

Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
